abstract: Deloitte's annual State of AI in the Enterprise survey of 3,235 director-to-C-suite leaders across 24 countries (fielded Aug-Sep 2025) finds AI moving from pilots to enterprise scaling, with worker access expanding 50% in one year. While productivity gains are widespread, only 34% of firms are using AI for deep business transformation, and 84% have not redesigned jobs around AI capabilities. The report also examines sovereign AI, agentic AI (74% plan deployment within two years), and physical AI trends.
keyFindings: Workforce access to sanctioned AI tools grew from under 40% to under 60% of workers in one year (among surveyed AI-using firms)
Only 25% of firms have moved 40%+ of AI experiments into production, but 54% expect to within 3-6 months
34% of firms are using AI for deep business transformation; 37% use AI at surface level with little process change
84% of companies have not redesigned jobs around AI capabilities despite high automation expectations
74% of companies plan to deploy agentic AI within two years, but only 21% have mature governance for autonomous agents
methodology: Survey of 3,235 director-to-C-suite respondents across 24 countries (Aug-Sep 2025). Industries: consumer, energy/resources/industrials, financial services, life sciences/healthcare, TMT, government/public services. All participating organizations had one or more working AI implementations. Supplemented by 15 qualitative interviews with global C-suite executives.
qualifiers: Survey sample is biased toward AI-active organizations (all had working AI implementations). Respondent pool is global (24 countries), not US-only. Self-reported data from senior leaders, not measured outcomes. Results reflect intentions and perceptions, not verified deployments.
